entities.name: Archias of Thurii
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Archias of Thurii, an actor from Magna Graecia turned ruthless military agent for the Macedonian general Antipater, played a pivotal role in the suppression of Athenian dissent following the Lamian War in the late 4th century BCE. Operating in the turbulent aftermath of Alexander the Great's death, Archias became notorious as the "hunter of the exiles" (φυγαδοθήρας), a moniker reflecting his grim efficiency in tracking down and eliminating prominent anti-Macedonian figures.

His most significant actions occurred in 322 BCE, when Antipater, having crushed the Greek rebellion, dispatched Archias to apprehend the leading Athenian orators who had fled the city. Archias successfully located and captured Hyperides from the temple of Aeacus on Aegina, delivering him to Antipater for execution. He also pursued Demosthenes to the temple of Poseidon on the island of Calauria, where the orator, rather than face capture and torture, famously committed suicide by poison. Archias's relentless pursuit effectively decapitated the anti-Macedonian political movement in Athens, silencing its most powerful voices and consolidating Antipater's grip on the city-state.

Archias's campaign of political assassination fundamentally altered the trajectory of Athenian autonomy, marking a definitive end to its golden age of independent political discourse. His actions served as a stark warning to other Greek cities contemplating resistance to Macedonian hegemony, demonstrating the brutal consequences of opposition. The swift removal of key figures like Demosthenes and Hyperides deprived Athens of experienced leadership and moral authority, contributing to its prolonged subjugation under Macedonian influence.

Though his precise end is unrecorded, Archias is said to have eventually died in poverty, a poignant and perhaps ironic twist for a man whose infamy was built on extinguishing the vibrant, defiant spirit of ancient Greece's most celebrated orators.
